How to choose crypto custody providers for institutional and tokenized assets
Custody decisions affect security, investor confidence, transfer authorization, compliance evidence, redemption workflows and whether institutions can approve a digital asset product.

Identify the exact contracting entity and who controls signing and recovery. A cryptographic method such as MPC does not, by itself, establish legal custody status. Ask your legal adviser which arrangements your project requires.

Use a sandbox transfer requiring two independent approvals. Try an unauthorised destination and an amount above the policy limit. Request the rejection reason, approver history and exported audit record.

Ask how a departed administrator, unavailable signing device or supplier outage is handled. Establish who holds recovery material, which parties must cooperate and how recovery is tested without exposing production keys.

Test a restricted token transfer, a failed transaction and a reporting export. Confirm the exact token contract and network, not only the asset ticker. Assign responsibility for reconciling wallet balances with your ownership records.

What is the difference between MPC and multi-signature custody?

MPC splits key material across parties without exposing a full private key, while multi-signature wallets require multiple separate signers on-chain. MPC is common for institutional operations; multi-sig is common for DAOs and transparent treasury controls.
